title: Tech Note: The 4D Language, Part 1: New Concepts in Version 6
author: Walt Nelson
featured_technology: 4D v6.0 language enhancements (longer names, constants, object properties, events)
4D as Web Server (early built-in web server feature)

historical_commentary.text: This note is a comprehensive preview of the 4D v6.0 language for developers upgrading from earlier versions, covering revised terminology (File to Table, Procedure to Method), longer object names (31 characters), built-in constants, hexadecimal/bitwise operators, BLOBs, object properties and events, expanded query limits/destinations, password-related commands, stored procedures, and 4D's then-new built-in Web Server capability. Nearly every specific feature described has since been superseded multiple times over: object names now support far more than 31 characters, the early built-in Web Server bears little resemblance to 4D's modern web server and web services stack, and stored procedures/passwords have been reworked repeatedly across two decades of subsequent 4D versions, making this note valuable mainly as a historical snapshot of the v6.0 transition rather than a current technical reference.
related_updates: 4D's object/table/field naming length limits have been increased far beyond the 31-character limit described here in subsequent versions

The early built-in Web Server feature introduced in 4D v6.0 has been completely re-architected multiple times since, culminating in the modern 4D Web Server, 4D REST/QODLY, and ORDA-based web technologies with no direct resemblance to this initial implementation
4D's terminology shift from 'File'/'Procedure' to 'Table'/'Method' documented here as new in v6.0 has long since become the sole, standard terminology used in all modern 4D documentation
BLOB handling, object properties/events, password commands, and stored procedures have all been substantially extended and modernized in the many 4D versions released since v6.0
